html:
Chiang Mai was founded in 1296 by King Mangrai as the capital of Lan Na, the kingdom of the northern Thai. Its name means new city.

Lan Na grew into a centre of Buddhist learning, with its own script and chronicles. Its temples, such as Wat Chedi Luang, held for a time the Emerald Buddha.

The Burmese of Bayinnaung took Chiang Mai in 1558 and ruled it for two centuries. After Siam drove them out in the late 18th century, Lan Na became a vassal and in the early 20th century part of Siam. Chiang Mai is now Thailand's second city of culture. See Chulalongkorn.
sum: Chiang Mai was founded in 1296 by King Mangrai as the capital of Lan Na, the kingdom of the northern Thai. Its name means new city.
